note: Closed variety of the tracker and the version-control host (FR-13): what a ticket key looks like and which commands deliver a change. Read by scripts/adapter_forms.py, the ONE reader; no other script holds a key shape or a delivery spelling. `ticket.kinds.<kind>`: `key` is a BARE regex (no capture group, never matches the empty text), `example` is what a person would write, `mentions` (optional) are extra ways a key is written in running text, each a regex with exactly one `({key})` group. A kind whose key never carries a project prefix (a bare number) is read as prefix-less: its keys count in free text only as `#N`, after `Ticket:` or through its own `mentions`, never as a bare number. `ticket.prefixless_mentions` are the mentions every prefix-less kind gets; `label` is the `Ticket: <key>` line the factory writes into every dispatch, which is the only mention that names a story (any form). `ticket.local` {key, example} is the key the factory gives a story no tracker holds (a bare regex like a kind's `key`, an example it takes whole); it is NOT a tracker kind, it is accepted under every kind, and a key of that shape is a local story only when its text file exists (scripts/local_keys.py, the ONE reader of that fact). `ticket.fallback_kind` is the form used when the project names no tracker, or names one this file does not hold and gives no `adapters.ticket.key_pattern`. `vcs.aliases` maps the program name a person may write to the host kind. `vcs.kinds.<kind>.delivery_commands` are the commands that deliver a change (open a merge or pull request): at least two whitespace-separated words, program first, or one word that is a push option. Every kind's commands are ALWAYS recognised, whatever the project's host is - a gate that knew only the configured host would let the other host's command through. A project adds its own through `adapters.vcs.delivery_commands`; the file is never narrowed by a config. `vcs.mention_commands` are the commands whose quoted arguments are text (a message, a pattern, an echo): a delivery command named inside them is a mention; the quoted arguments of every other command (ssh, eval, python -c, a shell) are read as commands again. `vcs.list_heads` are the words that open a list of words (`for`, `foreach`): substitutions standing alone in such a segment (`for f in $(a) $(b)`) are not read as the words of a delivery command, but a delivery word written in it, or a quoted argument, is read as before (`for c in "gh pr create"; do $c; done` runs it); a head that is a mention command or a bare `$var` releases pure substitutions the same way. `vcs.text_receivers` are the commands that only store, count or reorder what a heredoc or here-string hands them (`cat`, `tee`): a body written to one is text the stage guard does not read as a command, together with the receivers named by `vcs.mention_commands` and a script run; `vcs.script_runners` are launchers of a script file besides the python family of `launch-causes.json` (`run-py`), and `vcs.script_plain_flags` the flags of a python launcher that leave the script as the next word (`-B`, `-u`): a launch of a `.py` file reads its arguments as text, since the script may deliver with no words on the command line at all and the guard reads no script files. A damaged table gives none of the three lists, so nothing is then taken out of a command. A script that cannot read this file uses the built-in floor in adapter_forms.py (the Jira key shape, `glab mr create`, `gh pr create`) and says so.
